strengths: Clear and well-motivated problem formulation with compelling empirical evidence that retriever scores contain useful information and reranking acts as noise reduction (Figure 1 visualizations are particularly effective)
Principled theoretical grounding through variational inference framework; analytical decomposition (Eq. 3) clearly shows limitations of naive score incorporation
Comprehensive experimental validation including offline experiments on 3 datasets, online A/B testing on industrial platform with 1.089% realshow improvement, and extensive ablation studies (RQ1-RQ6)
Strong empirical results consistently outperforming state-of-the-art baselines including generator-evaluator and diffusion-based methods across all metrics
Generalization demonstrated across different reranker backbones (PRM, Pier), retrievers (MF, dual-tower), and improved diversity metrics
High reproducibility standards with detailed implementation details, hyperparameter settings, algorithm description, and promised code release
weaknesses: Theoretical gap: The δₓ term in Eq. (5) is acknowledged as 'not directly optimizable' but the paper provides no empirical analysis of whether it actually becomes small through optimization of other terms. This is a concerning theoretical loose end

Inconsistent online A/B test results (Table 11): while realshow improves (+1.089%), several metrics regress (watch-time -0.091%, share-rate -0.758%, save-rate -0.690%). The explanation about users 'exploring broader videos' is speculative and raises questions about whether the method optimizes for the right objectives

Heuristic generator design choices lack principled justification: Beta distribution selection is motivated only by conjugacy arguments; switching from heuristic to model-based generator at epoch λₑ appears to be a workaround for training instability rather than principled design

Method complexity with three additional hyperparameters (λc, λm, λe) requiring tuning beyond standard ML parameters; sensitivity analysis shows all matter significantly, complicating practical deployment
Incomplete baseline comparisons: missing recent retriever-aware reranker methods and learnable score fusion approaches; most baselines are reranker-only methods

Limited scope analysis: assumes continuous scores in [0,1], unclear how method handles discrete scores or ranking-only retrievers; retriever is fixed during reranker training limiting joint optimization; scalability with candidate pool size not discussed

Moderate novelty: individual components (adversarial learning, noise generation, variational bounds) are standard techniques; main novelty is their combination for reranking and the noise reduction perspective rather than fundamental algorithmic advances

Presentation clarity: heavy notation (x, x', xᵤ, x'ᵤ) can confuse readers; key algorithm details relegated to appendix; 'denoising' framing could be better motivated against alternatives like calibration or distribution matching
